    Set into the west wall of this natural cavern is a stone double door that is partly open. Bestial, high-pitched laughter echoes within.

    The gnolls rigged the door with a makeshift alarm.

    • Door Alarm. This simple alarm consists of armor scraps and rusty weapons balanced atop the partly open double door. Moving either door triggers the trap, the rules for which are as follows:

    • Avoiding the Trap. A Medium or smaller creature can slip through the gap between the doors with a successful DC 13 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check; failing this check triggers the trap.

    • Detect and Disable. As a Search action, a character can examine the door and make a DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check, detecting the trap on a successful check. Once detected, the trap can be disabled by a character who takes the Utilize action and succeeds on a DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check; failing this check triggers the trap.

    • Triggering the Trap. If the door is moved, the scraps clatter to the ground. The noise alerts all the gnolls in the cave, who cackle as they rush to dispatch intruders.

    J2: Junk Pile p24[−]

    p24[−]

    The center of this chamber's floor is piled with loose junk—broken ceremonial implements, rusty candlestick holders, and rotten rags.

    The gnolls piled objects here to sift through later.

    • DM Tip! If you increased this cave's difficulty, one or more Hostile Bugbear Warriors might be here rummaging through the junk.

    J3: Old Chapel p24[−]

    p24[−]

    This forlorn chapel is unfurnished, though a slightly depressed section of floor near the southeast wall suggests an altar or some other heavy object once rested there.

    Two tall warriors with mangy hides and hocked knees move about the chamber slowly, their hyena-like heads sniffing its walls.

    Two Gnoll Warriors scour this chamber for secret doors. The Hostile gnolls lunge at intruders in a frenzy. Combat in this chamber draws the attention of the gnolls in area J4, which quickly join the fray.

    If the characters defeat all but one gnoll, the last of them surrenders. As an Influence action, a character can try to cow the gnoll into submission and make a DC 13 Charisma (Intimidation) check. On a successful check, the gnoll's attitude improves to Indifferent, and the gnoll reveals that its pack was searching for "a prize hidden in the mouth of a laughing fiend." On a failed check, the gnoll flees without divulging any information.

    Olivier Bernard

    J4: Shrine of the Laughing Devil p25[−]

    p25[−]

    A stone dais spans much of the south wall of this eerie shrine. Above the dais, a mosaic of black and red tiles depicts the face of a laughing devil whose forked tongue curls down to the dais.

    Unless drawn elsewhere, two Gnoll Warriors pace about this chamber, frustrated in their fruitless search for treasure. The Hostile gnolls behave similarly to the pair in area J3; combat in this chamber draws those gnolls here.

    Illusory Wall. The laughing devil face is an illusory wall; it looks real to the eye but has no substance. A creature that touches the illusory wall discovers its true nature and can pass right through it.

    As a Study action, a character can make a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check to discern the wall's true nature. On a successful check, the character recognizes the wall is a magical illusion.

    J5: Hidden Crypt p25[−]

    p25[−]

    The devil's face ripples to reveal a dusty crypt. Ancient bones and rubble litter the tiled floor. An austere sarcophagus stands in each corner, and an ornate chest rests in the center of the room.

    Long ago, an evil mage reanimated the corpses of four explorers and commanded them to guard this crypt's treasure for all eternity. Entombed here are four Zombies, one in each sarcophagus.

    If the characters touch any of the sarcophagi or the chest, the Hostile zombies push the lids off their containers and start combat, seeking to rend intruders limb from limb.

    Helge C. Balzer

    Treasure. Among the debris is the skeleton of a human thief. The thief's purse contains 15 GP and a large gemstone (worth 100 GP).

    The chest is unlocked. It contains one magic item; roll once on the Magic Items table in appendix A (rerolling duplicates) to determine the item.

    K: Shrine of Evil Chaos p26[−]

    The Cult of Chaos performs evil rites in this cave, subtly drawing monsters to inhabit the Caves of Chaos and bring strife to the Borderlands. The current cult leader is Ivlis, the keep's former priest. Her cruel assistant, Narthus, is always here, and other cultists dwell close by (see cave G). Undead guardians defend the shrine and the Chaos Bell—the source of the cult's foul magic—at the shrine's heart.

    You can add monsters, such as Cultists, to the cave to make this scenario longer and more difficult, or you can reduce the number of Skeletons or Zombies to make the scenario easier and shorter.

    Dario Jelusic

    Getting Started p26[−]

    This cave is connected to cave G via the stairs east of area K5 (see map K). If the characters approach from outside the cave, read the following boxed text aloud to begin:

    p26[−]

    A foul draft issues from this cave. Red strata intertwine with bulging black veins running through the hewn rock. A sinister crimson light dances deep in the cave.

    The stench issues from the rotting ogre in area K2.

    Shrine Features p26[−]

    The cave has the following features:

    • Ceilings. The cave's ceilings are 20 feet high.

    • Doors and Secret Doors. Doors throughout this cave are made of heavy stone. The secret doors to area K8 blend in with their surroundings but are obvious from inside area K8. As a Search action, a character can make a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check to examine the wall for a secret door, noticing it on a successful check.

    • Environment. The cave instills a sense of unease in its visitors.

    • Lighting. Unless otherwise noted, Bright Light from red-flamed wall sconces fills the cave's areas.

    Shrine Locations p26[−]

    The following locations are keyed to map K.

    Marc Moureau
    Without Tokens
    Marc Moureau
    Player Version
    Marc Moureau

    K1: Entrance p26[−]

    Shadows shroud this foreboding entrance.

    K2: Guarded Hallway p26[−]

    Helge C. Balzer
    p26[−]

    The stench of death fills this hallway. Flies buzz around a groaning, slack-jawed giant backlit by red-flamed wall sconces.

    An Ogre Zombie conscripted by the cultists to guard their nefarious acts stands watch here, but the undead brute is easily fooled.

    The ogre zombie lets members of the Cult of Chaos pass unscathed, but it is Hostile toward entrants not garbed in the cult's attire and pummels them on sight. The creature is Indifferent toward anyone wearing a Cultist's Robe.

    K3: Chapel of Evil Chaos p26[−]

    Four pillars support the domed roof of this empty chapel, where cultists conduct foul ceremonies.

    • DM Tip! If you increased this cave's difficulty, two or more Hostile Cultists might be in the midst of an unholy ceremony here.

    K4: Undead Barrack p26[−]

    Four Zombies shamble restlessly in this bare chamber. They fight any non-Undead not garbed in the cult's attire but are Indifferent toward anyone wearing a Cultist's Robe.

    K5: Altar of Evil Chaos p26[−]

    David Auden Nash
    p26[−]

    Violet draperies curtain this chamber. Three stone altars stand before a dais topped with five chairs: four rickety seats made of bone flanking a high-backed throne. An ominous, black iron bell hangs from a stand near the middle of the room.

    Piles of humanoid bones are arranged neatly near the north wall. A cultist flecks the bones with blood while intoning a demonic chant.

    Narthus chants evil litanies in this impious chamber. He is Hostile toward the characters, even if they're garbed in cult attire; Narthus screens every new cultist and knows his fellow cult members well.

    If the characters interrupt the ritual, Narthus decries them as blasphemers and starts combat. On his turn, Narthus tries to ring the Chaos Bell, causing the bones to animate (see the "Chaos Bell" section).

    Chaos Bell. Hanging from the stand is the Chaos Bell, a profane relic whose toll can wake the dead.

    As a Bonus Action, a creature within 5 feet of the Chaos Bell can ring it, causing the bone piles to knit together and arise as four Hostile Skeletons. The tolling bell also summons the Zombies in area K4 to the fray. The skeletons and zombies obey Narthus's commands.

    Zoltan Boros

    The Chaos Bell is all but indestructible. To destroy the bell and end its magic, the characters must submerge it in the sacred spring (see the "Wilderness" section). If a character removes the bell from its stand, give that player the Chaos Bell.

    K6: Visitor's Chamber p27[−]

    This room has comfortable chairs and a low table. Cult leaders interview potential new recruits here.

    K7: Cult Leader's Room p27[−]

    p27[−]

    This opulent chamber contains a large bed, desk, and wardrobe. A ghastly demon head is mounted on the wall. Kneeling before the demon is a human woman wearing bloodred robes and a spidery headdress.

    Ivlis, leader of the Cult of Chaos, lives here. Each day, she pays tribute to the severed demon head mounted on the wall, which she talks to when no one's around. Ivlis is Hostile toward the characters.

    If confronted, Ivlis first tries to tempt the party with promises of untold riches and power, claiming all things are possible through the Cult of Chaos. She urges the characters to submit to the cult and become Undead. If they refuse, she fights.

    Diana Cearley

    Fighting Ivlis. In combat, the sneering cult leader fights arrogantly and doesn't hold back. If reduced to 15 Hit Points or fewer, however, she tries to flee the cave through area K8 via the secret door. If Ivlis escapes, she attempts to revive the cult elsewhere.

    Treasure. The demon head pivots to reveal a nook with 100 GP, a large red garnet (worth 100 GP), and two magic items; roll twice on the Magic Items table in appendix A (rerolling duplicates) to determine the items.

    K8: Secret "Treasure" p27[−]

    This hidden room contains only a black iron chest. When a creature moves within 5 feet of the chest, it springs open and spills 300 GP across the floor.

    Treasure. The coins are cheap counterfeits intended to slow greedy pursuers. A cursory examination of the coins reveals them as fakes.

    Conceptopolis

    Keep on the Borderlands p2[−]

    Rising from rugged crags amid a harsh countryside, the Keep on the Borderlands is a bastion of peace amid an otherwise brutal wilderness. The keep's stalwart defenders protect their community from the forces of chaos that would revel in its fall.

    DM Secret. This is for the Dungeon Master's eyes only. Unless text appears in a read-aloud box (like the one below), don't read it to the players.

    Chris Rallis

    Getting Started p2[−]

    The Keep on the Borderlands Map displays all the locations characters can visit in the keep. Share this map with your players.

    To begin, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p2[−]

    You ascend a winding road through a forested and mountainous country. Ahead, atop a sheer-walled stone plateau, looms a great and stoic keep. Armed sentries along the outer wall peer down at you, ready to welcome new heroes or repel would-be invaders.

    Two armed guards stand at the front gate. They hail you and motion for you to approach.

    The player characters start just outside the keep. The first time they arrive at the keep, the characters must proceed to the outer gatehouse (detailed later in this chapter), which functions as a tutorial with helpful sidebars. You can skip this location for subsequent visits to the keep unless the player characters want to return to it.

    After the characters visit the gatehouse or whenever they return to the keep, have the players choose a location shown on the map. The Keep Locations table summarizes noteworthy sites within the keep in the order they appear. Each location provides approximately 30–60 minutes of gameplay, depending on the nature of the characters' visit.

    Once the player characters choose a location, go to that location and review its "What You Need to Play" section.

    Keep Locations
    LocationDescription
    1: Outer GatehouseGuards vet entrants and keep watch at this gate.
    2: BarnLivestock and steeds are stabled and groomed here.
    3: Private ApartmentsThese modest apartments house long-term residents.
    4: SmithyA blacksmith crafts metalwork goods here.
    5: Provisioner's ShopThis messy, halfling-owned shop specializes in gear.
    6: Trader's ShopThis trading post sells armor and weapons.
    7: BankThe keep's citizens store their valuables at this bank.
    8: Traveler's InnTravelers can rent rooms at this cozy inn.
    9: TavernPatrons flock to this rowdy tavern for food and drink.
    10: Guild HouseMerchants and artisans assemble in this guildhall.
    11: TemplePriests offer guidance and healing in this house of worship.
    12: Inner GatehouseThis fortification is the keep's last line of defense.
    13: Inner BaileyThe keep's guards live and train in this enclosed court.
    14: FortressThe castellan governs the keep from this stronghold.

    Exploring the Keep p2[−]

    The player characters can visit any location in the keep, meeting and interacting with the citizens who reside there. Each keep location employs one or more NPCs, typically representing the most important person at a location, such as an establishment's owner or highest-ranking representative.

    The map of the keep isn't to scale, but you can use it to track the characters' current whereabouts. If this is your first time as Dungeon Master, ask your players to keep the party together; it's easier if the player characters visit each location as a group.

    Stacey Allan & William Doyle
    Player Version
    Stacey Allan & William Doyle

    Location Descriptions p3[−]

    Each description of a keep location has the following sections:

    • Features. This section details noteworthy features about the location.

    • NPCs. Each keep location contains one or more NPCs, each reflected by a digital NPC Card nested within the section.

    • Services. Services offered at the location, such as goods for sale or rooms for rent, appear here. If a player character pays for a good or service, collect Gold Pieces equal to its cost from that player.

    • Quest. This section contains a quest unique to the location. Most take place in the keep, though some encourage the characters to venture beyond its walls. Each quest can be completed only once.

    Social Interaction p3[−]

    The keep offers ample opportunities for characters to socialize with its inhabitants. All NPCs in the keep are initially Indifferent toward the characters. For more about NPC attitudes, see the D&D Beyond Basic Rules.

    Combat p3[−]

    Chris Rallis

    Combat is prohibited in the keep. If you need game statistics for an NPC, reference the recommended stat block listed on their NPC Card.

    At your discretion, characters who antagonize peaceful members of the keep might attract the attention of the soldiers of the keep, of whom there are many (use the Guard stat block). Those who refuse to keep the peace might be arrested and detained for a few days, fined up to 50 GP, or ousted from the keep until they can behave.

    The following stat blocks are used in this section:

    • Commoner
    • Curate
    • Gray Ooze Glob
    • Guard
    • Guard Captain
    • Knight
    • Noble

    Resting p3[−]

    Unlike in the other two adventure settings, the keep is a safe place to rest and resupply. The characters can freely take Long Rests in the keep. For more on resting, see the D&D Beyond Basic Rules.

    Leaving the Keep p3[−]

    The player characters can leave the Keep on the Borderlands whenever they choose. As they accumulate treasure and advance in level, the party might return to spend their hard-earned wealth, rest, or follow up on previously undertaken quests.

    Character Advancement p3[−]

    Though there are quests to complete in the Keep on the Borderlands, the characters don't gain levels in this section. Each quest offers its own reward, usually in the form of gold or favors.

    1: Outer Gatehouse p4[−]

    This gatehouse is the first stop for those seeking to enter the Keep on the Borderlands. The guards here greet outsiders, watch for potential threats, and permit entrance to citizens and peaceful visitors.

    p4[−]

    Summary. The beginning of each location summarizes its function in the keep and the NPCs who can be found at it. Don't read this aloud.

    When the characters arrive at the outer gatehouse, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p4[−]

    Two stone towers flank an archway that leads into the keep. A sturdy-looking gatehouse spans the archway and connects the towers. A wooden drawbridge allows passage over a steep ditch surrounding the keep. The bridge is currently drawn shut.

    Two guards stand before the raised bridge. As you approach, one of the guards shouts, "Hail! Do you bring peace or trouble?"

    p4[−]

    Boxed Text. Text that appears in a box like the one in this section is meant to be read aloud or paraphrased for the players when their characters first arrive at a location or under a specific circumstance, as described in the text.

    The guards are Bartho and Gala. The characters must respond to the guards and say whether they mean well or ill. After confirming the characters are well-meaning adventurers, Bartho and Gala call for the drawbridge to be lowered, then welcome the party to the keep.

    Bartho p4[−]

    Human Gate Guard

    • Statblock: Guard

    This gullible recruit spends more time dreaming than patrolling.

    • Distractable. Bartho is easily distracted from his post because he'd rather be doing anything else.

    • Sleepy. Bartho likes to catch a few winks during the night shift.

    1. Rumors
    2. "If you can't afford a bed at the inn, Cornflower will let you sleep in the barn. The hay's real comfy." (True)
    3. "Minotaurs aren't real. They're just a myth told to scare little children from wandering into caves." (False)
    Jane Katsubo

    Gala p4[−]

    Human Gate Guard

    • Statblock: Guard

    Though she's memorized all the keep's laws, this guard still has much to learn.

    • By the Books. Gala clings to the keep's laws—and often recites them aloud—whenever she must make a decision.

    • Naive. Gala believes that life is fair, people mostly tell the truth, and good always prevails.

    1. Rumors
    2. "I've heard the captain of the guard, Andrella, plans to retire soon." (False)
    3. "The keep's coat of arms honors its cavalry, thirty riders strong. I hope to become one." (True)
    Jane Katsubo
    p5[−]

    Social Interaction. Player characters can meet many different people throughout the keep. As DM, you assume the roles of these nonplayer characters, whom you can embody through either active or descriptive roleplaying (detailed below). Players also use one or both of these approaches to roleplay their characters.

    Regardless of the approach you prefer, use each nonplayer character's NPC Card to determine how they react to the character's words and actions.

    • Active Roleplaying. In active roleplaying, you speak with a character's voice and might echo their body language, like an actor taking on a role. You still need to describe things that can't reasonably be acted out.

    An active approach to roleplaying Bartho, an inexperienced guard prone to daydreaming, might involve you pretending to yawn mid-sentence or getting distracted by a butterfly. Perhaps he confides with the characters that he'd rather be doing something else.

    • Descriptive Roleplaying. In descriptive roleplaying, you draw on your mental image of the character, saying what the character does and how they do it.

    A descriptive approach to roleplaying Gala, a straitlaced guard who hopes to ascend in rank, might involve you describing her dutiful posture or no-nonsense expression. You might tell the players that she cautions the characters not to cause trouble as they enter the keep.

    Gatehouse Features p4[−]

    The gatehouse has the following features:

    • Drawbridge. The keep's first line of defense is a steep ditch, 10 feet wide and 10 feet deep, in front of the fortress. The only sure means to cross the dry moat is the drawbridge at this gatehouse.

    • Gate. The stone arch behind the drawbridge contains an iron portcullis and large oak doors.

    • Towers. Stairs inside each square, 30-foot-tall tower connect the ground floor to the roof. Arrow slits in the tower walls and roof battlements help archers defend the keep.

    p4[−]

    Features. Some features about a location help you set the mood or describe aspects of the location, while others detail important gameplay information, like the depth of the keep's moat (in case a creature falls into it).

    Banner for the Keep
    Coupleofkooks

    Gatehouse Services p4[−]

    The gatehouse offers the following services:

    • Lower the Drawbridge. The drawbridge usually remains raised night and day. To lower or raise the bridge, wheels in both towers must be turned to release or tighten the drawbridge's chains. The portcullis operates in a similar manner.

    p4[−]

    Services. Each location offers unique services. Shops typically offer goods for sale, which might be associated with a handout, while other locations offer more abstract benefits. An NPC at the location can summarize its services to the characters.

    • Orientation. The gate guards, Bartho and Gala, can describe and give directions to any location in the keep. They can also tailor recommendations to a traveler's needs. For example, if a character wants to purchase weapons or armor, the guards point them to the trader's shop (area 6).

    Quest: Entry Screening p5[−]

    Once the drawbridge is lowered, Bartho and Gala introduce themselves and encourage the characters to lend their services to the keep.

    p4[−]

    Exploration and Movement. Exploration is open-ended; the players don't take turns moving around the keep the way they do in combat. Instead, players simply say where they want their characters to go. None of the locations within the keep has or requires its own map; as DM, you help the players visualize these places through your descriptions.

    Read the following boxed text aloud:

    p5[−]

    "The keep has plenty of need for hearty adventurers like you," Gala says. "If you want to make a name for yourselves in this community and earn the castellan's respect, you should visit locations within the keep and offer your aid."

    "Residents usually pay for a job well done," Bartho adds casually.

    Before they venture into the Borderlands, the characters can report to the fortress (area 14) for more information on how they can further the interests of the castellan and his advisers.

    p5[−]

    Quest. Every location in the keep offers a quest: a heroic task or odd job intended for the party. The characters don't have to complete a quest at a location to benefit from its services. Unless stated otherwise, the characters can decline a quest; they can always return to complete it at a later time. Each quest's reward is stated at the end of its section.

    Bartho's Reward p5[−]

    The guards here have orders to help out around the keep between shifts, but Bartho claims he must rest instead to stay sharp when he's on duty. He pulls the characters aside and asks them to complete quests around the keep for a small reward.

    When the characters return to the outer gatehouse after completing at least three quests around the keep, Bartho thanks them and gives each character 5 GP.

    p5[−]

    Treasure. Rewards within the keep usually come in the form of Gold Pieces (GP). Whenever a player character finds gold, give that player Gold Pieces equal to the listed value, which is tracked on their character sheet. Encourage players to split their treasure as evenly as possible.

    2: Barn p6[−]

    This barn shelters the keep's livestock. It also serves merchants and travelers who need a place to stable their mounts while visiting the keep. Animals housed at the barn receive a box stall or pen, food, and grooming.

    When the characters arrive at the barn, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p6[−]

    Animals snuffle, cluck, oink, and moo inside the stalls of this spacious barn, which smells of leather and manure. A freckled halfling woman uses a pitchfork to unload hay from a nearby wagon into an empty stall. She wipes the sweat from her brow and extends a hearty greeting.

    The halfling is Cornflower, the barn hand.

    Cornflower p6[−]

    Halfling Barn Hand

    • Statblock: Commoner

    This spunky stable hand isn't afraid to get her hands dirty.

    • Animal Lover. Cornflower's best friends are all barn animals.

    • Idiomatic. Cornflower likes to use animal idioms, such as "busy bee," "chicken out," and "hold your horses."

    1. Rumors
    2. "Did you know animals have all sorts of special glands? Giant fire beetles are like big glowing cave lanterns! Isn't nature amazing?" (True)
    3. "Careful if you go trekking into the wilderness. The tamaracks are overrun with giant spiders." (True)
    Jane Katsubo

    Barn Features p6[−]

    The barn has the following features:

    • Box Stalls. The barn has roomy stalls for up to six Large mounts.

    • Livestock Pens. Cows, chickens, pigs, and other barn animals occupy several livestock pens.

    • Loft. Golden piles of hay are stored in a loft above the animal enclosures.

    • Trough. Stabled animals drink water from a common trough along the stalls.

    Barn Services p6[−]

    The barn offers the following services:

    • Chores. Once per day, the characters can assist Cornflower with chores around the barn, such as collecting freshly laid eggs, feeding and grooming animals, and milking cows and goats. In exchange for their help, Cornflower pays them 1 GP each.

    • Dairy Products. For 1 GP, Cornflower sells a pail's worth of milk or a slab of freshly churned goat butter (customer's choice).

    • Hit the Hay. Cornflower sympathizes with travelers who can't afford to stay at the inn (area 8). She lets them sleep in the loft for free.

    Quest: Billy Goat Wranglin' p6[−]

    After introducing herself and explaining the barn's services, Cornflower confesses she could use the characters' help. Read the following text aloud:

    p6[−]

    "Last night, I accidentally left the goat pen unlocked—and this mornin', all the goats were gone! I'm sure they're still within the keep, but I need to tend to the other animals here and make sure no others get loose. Would you track down the missin' goats and return them to the barn?"

    Cornflower offers the characters 1 GP for every goat they bring back. The number of missing goats equals the number of player characters.

    Finding the Goats p6[−]

    The goats are scattered throughout the keep. Roll 1d12 for each missing goat, rerolling duplicates. Keep these results secret. Each result corresponds to a numbered location on the Keep on the Borderlands Map where a goat can be found. For example, on a 6, a goat is outside the trader's shop (area 6). To find the goat, the characters must go to that location, though they don't have to venture inside.

    A character can narrow their search by making one of the following ability checks. Consider these examples:

    DC 10 Wisdom (Survival). The character follows hoofprints in the dirt.

    DC 10 Charisma (Persuasion). The character asks passersby if they've seen a loose goat.

    On a successful check, the character learns the location of one goat whose whereabouts the party doesn't already know.

    Returning the Goats p6[−]

    When the characters arrive at a goat's location, they find it grazing outside the structure and can coax it back to the barn. When the characters return a goat to Cornflower, she pays them 1 GP as thanks.

    A Spunky Barn Goat
    Jane Katsubo

    3: Private Apartments p7[−]

    Residents and long-term visitors rent apartments in this tenement building. The complex's most notable resident is also its landlord, a crotchety jeweler who invests in gemstones and other valuables.

    When the characters arrive at the apartments, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p7[−]

    A wooden jeweler's sign hangs over an open door in the front of this two-story building. Inside, an old human man hunches over a table, peering at an emerald through a jeweler's loupe.

    The jeweler, Lenk, puts down his loupe with a sigh and invites the characters in.

    Lenk p7[−]

    Human Jeweler

    • Statblock: Noble

    This elderly jeweler can identify and appraise any gemstone.

    • Faultfinder. Lenk has a knack for spotting flaws, be they in things or people.

    • Pessimistic. Lenk always sees the worst part of any situation.

    1. Rumors
    2. "Your money isn't safe at the bank. I hear a burglar broke in recently and stole every last coin." (Partially true; the burglar was unsuccessful)
    3. "Some stones hide things. The next time you're in an ancient dungeon or old cave, inspect the walls closely. You just might find a secret door." (True)
    Alexander Mokhov

    Apartments Features p7[−]

    The apartments have the following features:

    • Apartments. Each two-story apartment is a section of the same large tenement building. The apartments have identical amenities: a stove, a small drawing room, a bedroom, and a storage area.

    • Rain Barrel. A large barrel near the building holds clean water for washing dishes and clothes.

    Apartments Services p7[−]

    The apartments offer the following services:

    • Buy Gems. Lenk can buy gems the characters find in their adventures. Lenk exchanges gems at this location for their value in gold. All the gems in this adventure are worth 100 GP; this rate includes Lenk's appraisal fee.

    • Rent an Apartment. Characters can rent an apartment for 100 GP per month.

    Quest: Breaking the Bank p7[−]

    After detailing the services he offers, Lenk tells the characters he's exploring a new line of business. Read the following boxed text aloud:

    p7[−]

    "With reports of bandits along the trail and the occasional thief here in the keep, I plan to sell strongboxes to help citizens and travelers secure their valuables. I've received a few samples made by local crafters who hope to partner with me in this new venture, but I won't stake my reputation on shoddy handiwork.

    "I need to determine which of the strongboxes are fit for sale, and you look like a capable lot. Care to test your mettle on some metal?"

    If the characters agree, Lenk hands each of them a locked iron strongbox and instructs them to try to pilfer its contents however they please. Each strongbox contains a modest amount of gold. If a character can get into a strongbox, they can keep its contents, though Lenk doesn't reveal what's inside.

    Cracking the Strongboxes p7[−]

    A character can make one attempt to open a strongbox through any of the following means:

    • Breaking the Strongbox. Each strongbox is a Tiny object with AC 19, 5 HP, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and Vulnerability to Cold damage. A character who reduces a strongbox to 0 Hit Points with a single attack or spell destroys the strongbox but not its contents.

    Picking the Lock (A character who has Thieves' Tools). A character that can use Thieves' Tools to pick the strongbox's lock, doing so with a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.

    • Prying Open the Lid. A character can force open a strongbox's lid with a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.

    At the DM's discretion, other methods of opening a strongbox might exist.

    Reward p7[−]

    Inside each strongbox is 5 GP. If the characters manage to penetrate all the strongboxes, Lenk grouses about the boxes' poor craftsmanship. If all the strongboxes thwart their attempts, Lenk pays each character 1 GP as a consolation and says there are nobler skills to master than thievery.

    4: Smithy p8[−]

    The smithy is where the keep's residents purchase metal goods and have them repaired.

    When the characters arrive at the smithy, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p8[−]

    The smithy offers the following service:

    • Leather Branding. For 1 GP, Kalista can brand anything made of leather, such as Leather Armor or a Spellbook, with the keep's coat of arms.

    Quest: Tools of Destruction p8[−]

    If a character asks to purchase armor or weapons, Kalista explains why she no longer sells those to outsiders. Read the following boxed text aloud:

    p8[−]

    "I used to sell arms and armor to would-be heroes like you. I had heard reports of foolhardy adventurers falling victim to brigands and monsters. I shrugged those stories off for a time.

    "Last winter, the castellan's forces thwarted an assault on the keep. After the onslaught, I was sickened to learn that many of the attackers' weapons bore my maker's mark. By selling to outsiders, I had unwittingly armed our enemies. I vowed then never to forge another weapon for anyone but the keep's soldiers. I haven't since."

    The keep's soldiers occasionally bring confiscated weapons to Kalista for destruction.

    Weapon Smelting p8[−]

    Kalista recently received a cartload of battered and rusted weapons seized by the keep's defenders. She asks the characters to help melt them down.

    The disarmament process takes 1 hour. To aid Kalista with it, the characters must succeed on the following ability checks in this order:

    DC 13 Strength (Athletics). The character piles the weapons in the forge and undertakes the tough labor needed to properly melt them down.

    DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). The character carefully tips a crucible of molten metal into an ingot mold without spillage.

    If at least one character succeeds on each check, the party completes the disarmament. The characters can retry failed checks, but if they accumulate three failures, Kalista dismisses them with a sigh, insisting she can handle the rest of the job herself.

    If the characters successfully help Kalista destroy the weapons, she pays them each 5 GP.

    If the characters don't bring up the unusual sign on the storeroom door, Ruckus soon mentions it and asks for their help in resolving the matter. Read the following boxed text aloud:

    p9[−]

    "I've been smelling smoke in the storeroom for the past few days. Yesterday I peeked inside and saw a cloaked figure smoldering like an ember—surely it was a fire ghost! I threw a flagon of ale at it to put out the fire, but I haven't dared to enter the room since. Someone braver than me should lay the ghost to rest. Maybe you could do it?"

    The "Ghost" p9[−]

    The only thing haunting the shopkeeper is his own reckless disorganization. Ruckus recently relocated some inventory to a shelf in his storeroom; the merchandise included a hefty magnifying glass. On sunny days, the light through a high window focuses through the lens on a dusty old cloak, causing it to smolder. It's a major fire hazard.

    Ruckus's decision to leave the storeroom alone compounds the danger. If the problem isn't dealt with soon, a conflagration is inevitable.

    Investigating the Scene p9[−]

    Characters can get at the truth by investigating the jumbled storeroom, where they discover a singed cloak stained with dried ale.

    Gathering Clues. Characters in the storeroom can gather clues by succeeding on one of the following ability checks. Consider these examples:

    DC 13 Intelligence (Nature). At noon each day, sunlight from the window shines on the cloak.

    DC 12 Wisdom (Perception). High on a shelf near the storeroom window, a magnifying glass protrudes from an open box.

    Storeroom Box
    Axel Defois

    Solving the Case p9[−]

    After inspecting the storeroom, the characters can draw their conclusions. A character who considers the evidence and succeeds on a DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check correctly deduces the source of the smoke and the risk it poses to Ruckus's shop. A character who gathered one or both clues has Advantage on this check.

    If the characters explain the situation, Ruckus is relieved to hear his shop isn't haunted and corrects the fire hazard. As thanks, he pays each character 10 GP and encourages them to spend it here.

    Quest: Dangerous Stowaway p10[−]

    As the characters browse Oleira's wares, she offers them each 1 GP to unload a wagon while her sons are off watching soldiers train elsewhere in the keep. The delivery is late, so Oleira tells the characters to meet the wagon along the trail.

    Ooze Surprise p10[−]

    If the characters agree, the guards at the outer gate nod at them as they exit the keep and head down the trail. When the characters come across the wagon, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p10[−]

    A Gray Ooze Glob lurks within the abandoned wagon, waiting to ambush the characters. When the characters approach the wagon, the ooze seeps from the supplies with a hideous squelching noise and fights the characters. Roll Initiative!

    Preparing for Combat. Use the "Combat" section of the D&D Beyond Basic Rules, along with the Trail Map and the Gray Ooze Glob stat block, to run this encounter.

    After defeating the ooze, carting the goods is straightforward work. When the characters return to Oleira, she's shocked to learn of the ooze—she or her sons could've been seriously harmed.

    A Hefty Bank Deposit
    Coupleofkooks

    Quest: Bank Job p11[−]

    At the service counter, Quink asks the characters if they're adventurers looking for work. If they say yes, she leans in close and speaks to them in hushed tones. Read the following boxed text aloud:

    p11[−]

    "Yvette here is a lousy guard. There was a break-in recently on her watch, and the burglar got away. I fear the culprit might attempt another break-in, and I'd like you to prevent the heist—quietly. I can pay you a lump sum of twenty gold pieces for your services. What do you say?"

    If the characters accept, Quink continues:

    p11[−]

    "I'd like you to stake out the bank tonight. If you see a burglar trying to enter, intervene and convince the criminal to leave at once. Remember, I'm paying for discretion. If you try to give the thief a trouncing, it will no doubt cause a scene. I want this matter resolved without violence."

    Quink believes the culprit lives in the keep.

    Thief in the Night p11[−]

    That night, a masked thief stealthily approaches the bank's door and attempts to pick its lock. The thief is Indifferent toward and wary of the characters if approached but doesn't immediately run away.

    As an Influence action, a character can dissuade the thief and make one of these ability checks:

    DC 15 Charisma (Deception). The character tells the thief a lie, like saying the guards are coming.

    DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion). The character convinces the thief to pursue a different line of work.

    DC 15 Charisma (Intimidation). The character threatens the thief, who abandons the heist.

    On a successful check, the thief lingers long enough for the characters to recognize Yvette, the bank's usual guard! On a failed check, she flees before they can get a good look at her.

    Reward p11[−]

    Quink pays the characters 20 GP for stopping the heist as promised. If they also reveal the thief's identity, Quink is flabbergasted but adds a 10 GP bonus for the characters' exceptional work. Soon after, two guards arrive and arrest Yvette. After the arrest, Yvette no longer appears at this location.

    After making introductions, Haldryck tells the characters they look light on their feet and in possession of good manners. He could use their help. Read the following boxed text aloud:

On a failed check, the character still wakes the early riser but bumps a grumpy sleeper in the process, rousing them from their slumber. The characters must make this check three times, one for each early riser.

    Checking In with Haldryck p12[−]

    For waking the early risers, Haldryck rewards the party 5 GP, recommending they use it to rent a private room. If the characters completed the task without bothering any other guests, Haldryck gives the characters an additional 10 GP for their good work. Otherwise, he mutters about receiving a noise complaint from an unhappy guest.

    Quest: Chug Champion p13[−]

    The tavern's signature game is a nightly contest called chug champion.

    Playing the Game p13[−]

    To play chug champion, participants—called "chuggers"—line up at the bar and pay 5 GP each to receive three pints of either heady ale or non-alcoholic cider (their choice). The goal is to drink the pints as quickly as possible over 3 rounds.

    Each round, each participating character must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw to quaff the pint in one go. On a failed save, the character drinks too slowly and is eliminated along with a handful of other chuggers. Otherwise, they proceed to the next round. A character who succeeds on all three saves wins the game.

    If multiple characters succeed on all three saving throws, compare the results of those chuggers' last saves, rerolling any ties. The character with the highest result places first, the character with the second-highest result places second, and any other characters place third.

    A Tavern Stein
    Coupleofkooks

    Winning the Game p13[−]

    The winner receives 25 GP. Second- and third-place chuggers win 15 GP and 10 GP, respectively.

    Quest: Chaos Unfurls p14[−]

    Once Toryn learns the characters are adventurers, she tries to hire them. Read the following aloud:

    p14[−]

    "I recently received a shipment of tempestuous magical scrolls. I need them stored in special scroll cases. If you tackle this chore for me, I'll pay you a total of twenty gold pieces. Be warned: the scrolls have a will of their own."

    If the characters agree, Toryn leads them to a storeroom containing a pile of empty scroll cases and a warded chest that holds the scrolls. She instructs the characters to open the chest when they're ready, then wishes them good luck and departs hurriedly.

    A Dangerous Magical Scroll
    Coupleofkooks

    Ensorcelled Scrolls p14[−]

    When the characters open the chest, the scrolls erupt from it in a flurry of whirling parchment and shimmering ink. Roll Initiative.

    Each round on Initiative Count 10 (losing Initiative ties), the scrolls fold themselves into weapons and deliver brutal paper cuts. Each character must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 Slashing damage. A character reduced to 0 Hit Points by a scroll has the Unconscious condition but is Stable.

    There are two scrolls for every player character in the party. As an action, a character can try to stow a scroll in its case by succeeding on one of the following ability checks:

    DC 12 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand). The character deftly plucks a scroll from the air and puts it into a scroll case.

    DC 12 Intelligence (Arcana). The character pacifies a scroll with an arcane gesture, allowing it to be scooped up and peacefully stored.

    DC 12 Charisma (Intimidation). The character bullies a scroll, causing it to flee into a case.

    Case Closed p14[−]

    If the characters encase all the scrolls, Toryn pays them 20 GP as promised. If the scrolls knock out all the characters, Toryn finishes the task before tending to the party. The characters wake up in her office with 1 Hit Point each. When the characters come to, Toryn apologizes sheepishly for putting them in so much danger, then awards them 10 GP for their effort.

    • Trusting. Fazzir always assumes the best of people.

    1. Rumors
    2. "The keep's former priest, Ivlis, left a large collection of books on all matter of subjects—even occult rituals." (True)
    3. "Anyone entering the inner bailey is bound to cross paths with Shannik, sergeant of the guard. I think he's a little too hard on new recruits." (True)
    Hazem Ameen

    DM Secret. Ivlis secretly leads the Cult of Chaos, an evil cult that feeds on destruction and disarray. Her supposed religious journey is a cover for her occult activities, which are detailed in the "Caves of Chaos".

    Temple Features p15[−]

    The temple has the following features:

    • Alms Box. A stout pole near the temple's entrance holds a small box for visitors to leave donations. At any given time, the alms box contains 1d8 GP. The box is unlocked. A character who steals from the alms box must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on D20 Tests for the next 24 hours.

    • Sanctuary. This spiritual center can accommodate dozens of worshipers. Fazzir delivers sermons from the altar each dawn. His simple lessons appeal to a variety of religious traditions.

    • Underground Accommodations. Fazzir inhabits modest rooms in the temple's cellar. The cellar also contains two small spare rooms. Fazzir uses these rooms as infirmaries or guest quarters as circumstances demand.

    Temple Services p15[−]

    The Sacred Services Handout lists available goods and services. Give this handout to the players whenever they visit this location. Fazzir provides the temple's healing and revival services as detailed on the Curate stat block.

    Sacred Services
    ServiceCost
    Flask of Holy Water25 GP
    Healing50 GP
    Revival2,000 GP
    Sacred Services Handout

    May all who act with kindness and virtue Always stand upright.

    May neither claw nor steel nor darkness hurt you; Be shielded by the light.

    Quest: Priestly Duties p15[−]

    In Ivlis's absence, Fazzir is having trouble keeping up with the flood of new responsibilities. He asks the characters to help him with two clerical tasks.

    A Holy Symbol
    Robson Michel

    Impromptu Blessing p15[−]

    A married couple asked Fazzir to give them a blessing for safe travel for a romantic getaway. Fazzir needs two assistants to perform the ceremony.

    To conduct the ceremony properly, two characters must each take the Study action and make a DC 10 Intelligence (Religion) check. On a successful check, the couple departs the temple with cheer. On a failed check, the couple postpones their trip, uneasy about what their journey might bring.

    Occult Symbol p15[−]

    Last night, a vandal defaced the temple with a strange symbol. Fazzir doesn't recognize the symbol. He asks the party to scrub away the graffiti.

    A blood-red bell is splattered onto the side of the temple in runny paint. A character who inspects the symbol and succeeds on a DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana) check recognizes the bell as the mark of the Cult of Chaos and an omen of future turmoil. If informed about the symbol's meaning, Fazzir finds the revelation deeply troubling. The mark washes off easily, but its stain on the priest's mind lingers.

    Reward p15[−]

    After these tasks, Fazzir gives each character 3 GP regardless of their performance. He is just grateful for their support.

    Good-Faith Discounts p15[−]

    It's unlikely that the characters will accumulate the gold required to revive a party member. At the DM's discretion, Fazzir might waive any of the fees on the Sacred Services Handout for those he believes show heroic potential.

    12: Inner Gatehouse p16[−]

    This gatehouse houses on-duty soldiers and separates the civilian areas of the keep from the inner bailey (area 13).

    When the characters arrive at the inner gatehouse, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p16[−]

    This gatehouse consists of a broad stone archway framed by a squat building constructed along the keep's inner wall. Battlements line its flat roof, atop which two guards stand watch.

    The guards ask the characters about their business, then escort them to Andrella, Captain of the Guard.

    Andrella p16[−]

    Human Captain of the Guard

    • Statblock: Guard Captain

    This captain is strong, stern, and just.

    • Perfect Posture. Andrella is as strict with her posture as she is with the law.

    • Role Model. Many of the keep's young people admire Andrella and enjoy her goodhearted mentorship.

    1. Rumors
    2. "A dastardly bandit, Pral, accosts travelers along the trail. Apparently he's quite handsome; I'm sure he'll look even better behind bars." (True)
    3. "The castellan tells me monsters are drawn to the Caves of Chaos in droves. I wonder why." (True)
    Zuzanna Wuzyk

    Gatehouse Features p16[−]

    The gatehouse has the following features:

    • Garrison. Twenty-four soldiers, including Captain Andrella, are garrisoned in the gatehouse.

    • Gate. The gate features a massive oak double door. During invasions, soldiers can bar the doors with a heavy timber beam from the other side.

    • Murder Holes. Guards atop the gatehouse can thrust spears down at invaders through holes in the ceiling of the archway.

    Gatehouse Services p16[−]

    The gatehouse offers the following service:

    • Requisition Uniforms. Characters who pledge to defend the keep can requisition uniforms from Andrella free of charge. Give those players one Borderlands Tabard each.

    A Rack of Standard-Issue Spears
    Alejandro Pacheco

    Quest: Testing the Defenses p16[−]

    Andrella has an unusual request. Once she learns the characters are adventurers, she dismisses the guards and says the following to the party:

    p16[−]

    "I want to observe how my soldiers would fare in an invasion scenario. As adventurers, you might be able to simulate such a threat.

    "I'd like you to sneak past the guards stationed here after sunset and steal a pennant from the other side of the gate. As part of this exercise, you can't harm any on-duty soldiers, but I'll explain the situation if any of you are detained. "Are you up for the challenge?"

    In exchange for their work, Andrella offers the characters a total of 25 GP.

    Infiltrating the Guardhouse p16[−]

    During the night, eight soldiers stand watch outside the gatehouse: six on the roof and another two on the ground before the open gate. If necessary, use the Guard stat block to represent each soldier.

    As an action, a character can try to bypass the soldiers and make one of these ability checks:

    DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth). The character slips past the soldiers undetected.

    DC 15 Strength (Athletics). The character scales the keep's sheer wall between regular patrols.

    DC 15 Charisma (Deception). The character fools the soldiers with a disguise or convincing lie.

    On a successful check, the character bypasses the soldiers undetected. On a failed check, two soldiers spot the character and take them into custody, but other characters can continue the mission.

    Debrief with Andrella p16[−]

    If at least one character reaches the pennant without getting caught, Andrella meets them afterward. She pays the party 25 GP as promised. If no characters were spotted, Andrella throws in an extra 15 GP and chastises the soldiers they evaded.

    If all the characters are detained before anyone in the party can grab the pennant, Andrella visits the characters in a sparsely furnished detention cell and thanks them for testing her soldiers. She informs the soldiers about the training exercise and smugly pays the characters 25 GP on their release.

    13: Inner Bailey p17[−]

    The sheltered inner bailey is where the keep's defenders live and practice combat drills.

    When the characters arrive at the inner bailey, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p17[−]

    Targets and practice dummies dot this courtyard, which contains a large stable and poles with hanging rings. Cavalry soldiers train atop horseback while guards watch the area from the walls and towers that rise around it.

    A mountain of a man in heavy armor tromps up to you. "No lollygagging!" he grouses.

    The man is the keep's demanding and curmudgeonly sergeant of the guard, Shannik.

    Shannik p17[−]

    Human Sergeant of the Guard

    • Statblock: Guard Captain

    Captain Andrella's second in command brooks no evildoers.

    • Brusque. When Shannik can substitute a reply with a grunt, he does so.

    • Shortsighted. Shannik's plans and actions fail to account for long-term repercussions.

    1. Rumors
    2. "An adventurer is only as good as their gear. Oleira at the trader's shop is a friend of mine. She can sell you armor and weapons." (True)
    3. "A real soldier can sleep off any injury. After a battle, I usually rent a bed at the inn. I always sleep better there." (True)
    Zuzanna Wuzyk

    Inner Bailey Features p17[−]

    The inner bailey has the following features:

    • Cavalry Stable. The bailey contains a stable with thirty horses. These war-trained horses serve as mounts for the keep's cavalry.

    • Guard Towers. Four towers rise above the bailey, one in each corner. The smallest, to the southeast, holds up to eight guards. The southwest and northeast towers each hold one dozen guards, as well as food stores and other supplies. The Great Tower to the northwest is 60 feet tall.

    • Watches. Eight soldiers, two atop each tower, watch over the inner bailey at all hours. Use the Guard stat block for these soldiers if necessary.

    Inner Bailey Services p17[−]

    The inner bailey offers the following service:

    • Weapon Upgrade. The keep ordered too many crossbows, which untrained recruits can't wield effectively. Shannik wants to trade the weapons for simpler ones. In exchange for 25 GP and a Shortbow, he can provide a character with a Hand Crossbow.

    Quest: Shannik's Chores p17[−]

    Shannik hires the characters to complete a couple chores around the inner bailey. The characters can refuse his request, but Shannik asks with increasing insistence each time they visit the inner bailey.

    Disrupting the Charge p17[−]

    Shannik wants to train two green recruits for the cavalry. He has them ride around the bailey for 10 minutes, spearing the hanging rings with lances.

    During the exercise, Shannik asks the characters to disrupt the training by distracting the horses or their riders without causing injury to either. A character can do so by succeeding on one of the following ability checks. Consider these examples:

    DC 13 Wisdom (Animal Handling). The character guides a horse off course.

    DC 13 Charisma (Intimidation). The character tries to startle a horse or its rider.

    A Cavalry Lance Laden with Training Rings
    Luca Bancone

    Catapult Installation p17[−]

    Shannik wants to install a catapult atop the Great Tower to defend against invaders. To do so, the characters must succeed on the following ability checks in this order:

    DC 15 Strength (Athletics). The character hauls supplies out of the stores in the southwest tower, across the bailey, and up the Great Tower.

    DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation). The character correctly assembles the catapult according to its blueprints.

    DC 13 Wisdom (Perception). The character calibrates the catapult by test-firing it at a target outside the keep's walls.

    This task takes 1 hour. If at least one character succeeds on each check, the party completes the task. The characters can retry failed checks, but if they accumulate three failures, Shannik dismisses them, grumbling about their incompetence.

    Reward p17[−]

    In exchange for completing a chore, Shannik pays a character 5 GP. A character can complete each of Shannik's chores only once. Thereafter, the sergeant greets the characters with a respectful nod whenever they visit this area.

    14: Fortress p18[−]

    The castellan governs the keep from its fortress, a stone stronghold solidly built to withstand assault. Multiple towers rise above the main building, which is 30 feet tall. The fortress shelters emergency resources, municipal chambers, and the keep's armed forces. Militaristic banners and upholstered furniture decorate its dignified interior.

    When the characters arrive at the keep fortress, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p18[−]

    Two round towers with pointed roofs flank this tiered stronghold. Archers march along its stone parapets, watching for signs of trouble. Two guards stand outside the fortress's iron doors; they acknowledge passersby with stern nods.

    Fortress Features p18[−]

    The fortress has the following features:

    • Armory. Barding and lances for the keep's cavalry—thirty troops strong—are stored here, though the equipment is off-limits to the characters.

    • Barracks. Sparsely furnished quarters throughout the fortress can collectively accommodate up to thirty-six soldiers at once.

    • Great Hall. A spacious hall in the fortress hosts ceremonies, proclamations, and other receptions.

    • Private Chambers. Two lavishly decorated rooms are reserved for guests of the keep, while another belongs to the castellan.

    • Towers. Two peaked towers rise from the fortress.

    • Undercroft. Beneath the fortress are cellars containing vast provision stores, a cistern, and a dungeon with four stout cells for detainees and prisoners. If Yvette was arrested at the bank (see area 7), she is detained in one of the cells.

    Fortress Services p18[−]

    The fortress offers the following services:

    • Defense. In times of crisis, the castellan can muster up to thirty-six trained soldiers from the fortress to defend the keep. The fortress also provides refuge during incursions.

    • Seat of Government. During the day, the castellan and his two assistants conduct business in the main building, where they hold audience with citizens and visitors of the keep.

    Quest: Official Errands p18[−]

    Each official in the fortress spurs the characters to explore a different adventure setting.

    Dwern the Scribe p18[−]

    The castellan's scribe, a dwarf man named Dwern, sits at a tidy desk in an austere office, documenting changes to the keep's inventory in a heavy ledger.

    When the characters visit Dwern, he issues the following quest:

    [−]

    "I've commissioned a map of the wilderness beyond the keep. However, the map is sorely lacking in detail, and few are willing to brave the wilds to properly survey them—but you look like you're made of sterner stuff.

    "If you help me finish my map by exploring the surrounding lands, I'll compensate you fairly."

    If the characters explore three or more wilderness regions (see the "Wilderness" section) and report their findings to Dwern, the scribe pays them a handsome reward: a large, glittering gemstone (worth 100 GP), which they can sell to the jeweler for gold (see area 3).

    Dwarf Scribe

    • Statblock: Noble

    This gruff scribe prefers the company of books over people.

    • Bookworm. Dwern has read more books than anyone else in the keep.

    • Curmudgeonly. Dwern is ill-tempered toward younger people—which, to him, are most people.

    1. Rumors
    2. "The guild house's library boasts a modest but impressive collection of books on history and magic." (True)
    3. "There's an ancient statue somewhere in the forests north of the keep. It was once the site of strange rituals. Some say it still is." (True)
    Svetlin Velinov

    "While Castellan Winvarle protects the keep from outside threats, it's my duty to preserve the peace within its walls and ensure its citizens are content.

    "I'd like you to visit a few businesses within the keep and help their owners with any odd jobs they might have. I recently acquired an item of arcane significance. Assist me in this effort, and the item is yours."

    If the characters complete three quests within the keep and report back to Elandra, she rewards them with one magic item; roll once on the Magic Items table in appendix A (rerolling duplicates) to determine the item.

    3. "Kalista, the keep's blacksmith, doesn't sell weapons to adventurers. If you want to know why, ask her." (True)
    Katerina Ladon

    Winvarle p18[−]

    Human Castellan

    • Statblock: Knight

    The keep's noble commander leads his soldiers whenever the keep comes under attack.

    • Idealistic. Winvarle's ideals are rooted in lofty notions of righteousness.

    • Oblivious. While he excels at battle strategy, Winvarle scarcely knows the inner workings of his own keep.

    1. Rumors
    2. "The Cult of Chaos is an affront to all that is good." (True)
    3. "Anyone can pledge to defend the keep. Talk to Andrella in the inner gatehouse if you'd like to join the keep's defenders." (True)
    Katerina Ladon

    Winvarle the Castellan p18[−]

    The keep's noble castellan, a human man named Winvarle, holds court daily in the great hall. A keen strategist, Winvarle casts his vigilant gaze toward the Caves of Chaos, where rumors of a sinister cult have surfaced (see the "Caves of Chaos").

    When the characters visit Winvarle, he issues the following quest:

    p19[−]

    "Your arrival is fortuitous. I've heard whispers of a nefarious cult—the self-proclaimed Cult of Chaos—that reportedly operates in a cave network to the northeast. I believe the source of the cult's power resides in one of those caves.

    "These lands yearn for heroes. For the good of the Borderlands and the people under my charge, I humbly ask you to investigate these rumors and, if need be, quash this evil before it reaches the keep."

    Winvarle claims this quest is its own reward, but he adds that the Caves of Chaos abound with treasure, hoping to entice any characters who seek only to fill their coffers.

    Castellan Winvarle also encourages the characters to meet with his adviser and scribe, who might have other tasks for them to complete.

    Heroes' Return p19[−]

    Castellan Winvarle and the citizens of the keep celebrate the characters' heroic deeds
    Katerina Ladon

    If the characters return to this location at level 3, having fulfilled all three keep officials' quests (detailed in the previous sections), they receive a heroes' welcome. That evening, Castellan Winvarle throws a celebration in the characters' honor and invites the citizens of the keep to participate in the festivities. At your discretion, any of the NPCs within the keep might be present at the celebration to mingle with the characters and show their appreciation.

    At the height of the revelry, the castellan publicly thanks the characters and presents them a writ of congratulations. Give the players the Castellan's Letter Handout, which might inspire future adventures involving the Keep on the Borderlands.

    Castellan's Letter Handout
    p19[−]

    Noble Adventurers,

    I extend to you my deepest thanks. Your gallant efforts have forestalled the forces of chaos and made the Borderlands a safer place. Where there was once uncertainty, there is now hope.

    Through your valiant deeds, you have proven yourselves to be more than mere mercenaries or vagabond explorers—you are heroes of the highest caliber. You have done an incredible service to the citizens of this keep, ensuring they can prosper in peace.

    As a token of my appreciation, I have reserved a chamber in the fortress for you. You and your companions may come and go in the keep as you please. Henceforth, consider it a base from which you can embark on future adventures, no doubt for the betterment of these lands and the people who call them home.

    Gratefully,

    Winvarle

    Castellan of the Keep

    Ending the Adventure p19[−]

    Castellan Winvarle's celebration marks the end of this adventure, but there's still plenty to explore after that. The characters can continue to adventure in the Keep on the Borderlands, the Caves of Chaos, and the Wilderness (detailed in each respective section) until they've experienced all the Borderlands has to offer. You can also use them to tell stories of your own.

    If you wish to advance these characters beyond level 3 and create new adventures for them, you need the core rules: the Player's Handbook, the Dungeon Master's Guide, and the Monster Manual.

    Chris Rallis

    Wilderness p2[−]

    The wilds of the Borderlands teem with dangerous animals and ravenous monsters.

    DM Secret. This is for the Dungeon Master's eyes only. Unless text appears in a read-aloud box (like the one below), don't read it to the players.

    Ignatius Budi

    Getting Started p2[−]

    The Wilderness Map displays all the regions characters can visit in this section of the adventure. The player version of this map doesn't reveal the contents of each wilderness region, only the general geographic features. Share that map with your players. The Caves of Chaos and the Keep on the Borderlands aren't labeled on this version of the map so the players don't confuse them with wilderness regions.

    To begin, read the following boxed text aloud:

    p2[−]

    Your adventuring party enters the wilderness. Mysteries await you in this untamed land. Where do you want to go?

    The Wilderness Regions table summarizes the regions in the order they appear within this section. If fully explored, each region provides about 60–90 minutes of gameplay.

    Each region is roughly the same difficulty, but the Trail region functions as a tutorial with helpful sidebars. If this is your first time as the DM, encourage the players to start there. Otherwise, have them choose a region shown on the map.

    Once the player characters choose a region, go to that region and review its "What You Need to Play" section.

    Wilderness Regions
    RegionDescription
    1: TrailFriendly travelers and no-good bandits alike use this dirt road.
    2: WoodsThese majestic forests shelter wily fey and occult secrets.
    3: FensTerritorial lizardfolk and a spy for hire lurk in this wetland.
    4: Tamarack StandGiant spiders plague this vast stand of conifers.

    Exploring the Wilderness p2[−]

    Wilderness encounters occur across large tracts of unmapped backcountry. The text tells you when to use a map and monsters; otherwise, you can resolve encounters using words and imagination.

    Stacey Allan & William Doyle
    Unlabeled Version
    Stacey Allan & William Doyle
    Player Version
    Stacey Allan & William Doyle

    Region Descriptions p2[−]

    Each description of a wilderness region has the following sections:

    • Features. Important features about the region, such as its lighting, appear here. The text assumes the characters explore the wilderness during the day and camp or return to the keep at night.

    • Getting Started. This section provides setup instructions for the DM and introduces the region to the characters with thematic read-aloud text.

    • Encounters. This section presents encounters that might occur in the region. Each encounter's text details what challenge the characters must overcome.

    Combat p2[−]

    Some encounters pit the characters against foes that mean them harm, such as wild animals or greedy bandits. See the D&D Beyond Basic Rules for how to run a combat encounter.
